easy.explanation: Samson went to Gaza.
easy.q: To what city did Samson go?

answers: At the gate of the city
easy.explanation: They waited for him all night in the gate of the city.
easy.q: Where did the Gazites lie in wait for Samson?

easy.explanation: Samson arose at midnight.
easy.q: When did Samson arise and take the city gate?

answers: To lead him to the mountain
medium.explanation: They planned to seize and kill him in the morning.
medium.q: Why did the Gazites wait all night for Samson?

answers: He opened it and left it in place
He took it away, bar and all
medium.explanation: He took the doors, posts, and bar and carried them away on his shoulders.
medium.q: What did Samson do with the city gate?

medium.explanation: The Gazites remained quiet while secretly waiting for morning.
medium.q: What does “were quiet all the night” mean in this context?

answers: Samson arose at midnight and acted before them
challenge.explanation: Samson arose before the time they had planned to kill him.
challenge.q: Why did the Gazites’ plan fail?

answers: That he disguised himself as a Gazite
That he wanted to hide in the city
challenge.explanation: Carrying away the city gate shows Samson’s exceptional strength.
challenge.q: What does Samson’s carrying the gate to the mountain demonstrate?

challenge.explanation: The verse says the hill was before Hebron.
challenge.q: The mountain was before which place?

paragraphs.title: Delilah and the First Attempt to Capture Samson

easy.explanation: Samson loved a woman named Delilah.
easy.q: Whom did Samson love?

easy.explanation: Delilah lived in the valley of Sorek.
easy.q: Where was Delilah?

easy.explanation: They offered her eleven hundred pieces of silver each.
easy.q: What did the lords of the Philistines offer Delilah?

answers: Where his great strength lay and how he could be bound
medium.explanation: They asked her to entice him and find how he could be bound.
medium.q: What did the Philistine lords ask Delilah to discover?

answers: Because she was a Philistine ruler
Because she guarded the city gate
medium.explanation: Samson loved Delilah, so they used her to question him.
medium.q: Why did the Philistines approach Delilah?

medium.explanation: They wanted Delilah to deceive Samson and learn the secret of his strength.
medium.q: What does “entice him” mean in this passage?

answers: His love allowed her to come close and question him
His love caused him to leave Gaza
His love made her an enemy of the Philistines
challenge.explanation: Because Samson loved her, Delilah had access to him and could question him.
challenge.q: What connection existed between Samson’s love for Delilah and the danger facing him?

answers: They wanted to purchase the city
They were willing to pay to capture Samson
challenge.explanation: They offered Delilah money in exchange for discovering how to bind him.
challenge.q: What does the offer of silver reveal about the Philistines’ purpose?

answers: To ask him how he might be bound
To bring him to Dagon’s temple
challenge.explanation: Delilah began by asking about the source of his strength and how he could be bound.
challenge.q: What was the first step in Delilah’s plan?

easy.explanation: Samson said that seven green withs would bind him.
easy.q: What was Samson’s first answer?

answers: His hair woven into a loom
easy.explanation: He said that new ropes could bind him.
easy.q: What was his second answer?

answers: Samson broke free and broke the restraints
easy.explanation: Each time Samson broke the restraints and escaped.
easy.q: What happened in each attempt?

answers: She bound him with seven green withs
medium.explanation: Delilah bound him with seven green withs that had not been dried.
medium.q: What did Delilah do after Samson gave his first answer?

answers: They were all false ways of binding him
medium.explanation: Samson gave false answers, and he escaped each time.
medium.q: What did Samson’s first three answers have in common?

medium.explanation: The ropes came off his arms as easily as a thread breaks.
medium.q: What does “as a thread” convey in the description of Samson’s escape?

answers: She repeatedly tried different ways of binding him
She immediately appealed to his brothers
challenge.explanation: After each answer, she tested the suggested method of binding him.
challenge.q: How did Delilah’s attempts to learn Samson’s secret progress?

answers: The Philistines prepared to seize Samson immediately
challenge.explanation: The men were ready nearby to capture Samson if the method worked.
challenge.q: What does the presence of men lying in wait show?

answers: His seven locks would be woven with the web
Seven cords would be tied around him
The city gate would be tied to him
challenge.explanation: Samson said that weaving the seven locks of his head with the web would bind him.
challenge.q: What was Samson’s third answer?

paragraphs.title: The Secret Revealed and Delilah’s Betrayal

answers: Where he would take the gate
easy.explanation: Delilah demanded that Samson reveal the source of his strength.
easy.q: What did Delilah want Samson to tell her?

answers: That he was a Nazarite unto God and his hair had never been shaved
That his strength came from ropes
easy.explanation: He told her that he was a Nazarite and that shaving his hair would remove his strength.
easy.q: What did Samson finally reveal?

answers: She called for the Philistine lords
She sent him to his father’s house
easy.explanation: Delilah sent and called for the Philistine lords.
easy.q: What did Delilah do after Samson revealed his secret?

answers: Delilah pressed and urged him day after day
medium.explanation: Delilah pressed him daily until his soul was vexed unto death.
medium.q: What caused Samson to reveal all his heart?

medium.explanation: The passage says that his strength went from him.
medium.q: What happened after Delilah shaved the seven locks of Samson’s head?

medium.explanation: Delilah continually pressured Samson until he gave in.
medium.q: What does “she pressed him” mean in this context?

answers: His hair was connected with the sign of his consecration and his strength
His hair enabled him to open gates
challenge.explanation: Samson said he was a Nazarite and that shaving his hair would cause his strength to leave him.
challenge.q: What was the connection between Samson’s hair and his Nazarite vow?

answers: That the Lord was departed from him
That Delilah was in the room
challenge.explanation: He expected to escape as before, but did not know that the Lord had departed from him.
challenge.q: What did Samson not know when he awoke after his hair was shaved?

answers: She called the Philistines after he revealed his secret
challenge.explanation: She summoned the Philistines immediately after learning his secret.
challenge.q: Which detail especially emphasizes Delilah’s betrayal?

easy.explanation: The Philistines put out Samson’s eyes.
easy.q: What did the Philistines do to Samson’s eyes?

easy.explanation: He did grind in the prison house.
easy.q: What was Samson forced to do in prison?

easy.explanation: They offered a great sacrifice to Dagon their god.
easy.q: For which god did the Philistines celebrate?

answers: They believed their god had delivered Samson into their hands
medium.explanation: They said that their god had delivered their enemy into their hands.
medium.q: Why did the Philistines rejoice at their celebration?

answers: It was woven into a loom
medium.explanation: The passage says that the hair of his head began to grow again.
medium.q: What began to happen to Samson’s hair?

answers: Entertain them so they could mock him
medium.explanation: They brought Samson out so they could laugh at and mock him.
medium.q: What does “make us sport” mean in this context?

answers: His hair began to grow again
challenge.explanation: The verse notes that his hair began to grow after it was shaved.
challenge.q: What change in Samson’s condition is mentioned before the celebration?

answers: The event was small and private
The celebration was public and crowded
The Philistines were fleeing the building
challenge.explanation: About three thousand men and women watched from the roof.
challenge.q: What does the large number of people on the roof show?

answers: As the destroyer of their country who had slain many of them
As the builder of the temple
challenge.explanation: They called him their enemy and the destroyer of their country who had slain many.
challenge.q: How did the Philistines describe Samson?

easy.explanation: Samson asked the lad to let him feel the pillars upon which the house stood.
easy.q: What did Samson ask the lad to do?

easy.explanation: Samson called unto the Lord and asked for strength.
easy.q: To whom did Samson pray before his final act?

easy.explanation: He took hold of the two middle pillars.
easy.q: Between what did Samson stand?

answers: That he might be strengthened one more time
That his brothers would be sent
medium.explanation: He asked God to strengthen him only this once.
medium.q: What did Samson ask of the Lord?

answers: The house fell upon the lords and the people
medium.explanation: The house fell upon the Philistine lords and all the people inside.
medium.q: What happened when Samson bowed himself with all his might?

answers: He took hold of them and leaned upon them
He moved them away from the house
medium.explanation: He held the two pillars and used them to bring down the house.
medium.q: What did Samson do with the pillars?

answers: They were fewer than those he killed in life
They were more than those he killed in life
No one was inside the house
challenge.explanation: The dead he slew at his death were more than those he slew in his life.
challenge.q: What does the verse emphasize about the number who died with Samson?

answers: They led to the prison house
challenge.explanation: The house was supported by the pillars, so bringing them down caused the structure to fall.
challenge.q: Why was it important for Samson to reach the middle pillars?

answers: He asked for strength and then acted against the pillars
He prayed after the house fell
He prayed to save the Philistines
challenge.explanation: He first asked the Lord for strength and then took hold of the pillars.
challenge.q: What connection is there between Samson’s prayer and his action?

answers: His brethren and all his father’s house
easy.explanation: His brethren and all the house of his father took him and buried him.
easy.q: Who carried Samson to his burial?

easy.explanation: He was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol.
easy.q: Where was Samson buried?

easy.explanation: The verse says that Samson judged Israel twenty years.
easy.q: How many years did Samson judge Israel?

answers: In the buryingplace of Manoah his father
In the tomb of the Philistine lords
In a tomb at the city gate
medium.explanation: He was buried in the buryingplace of Manoah his father.
medium.q: In whose buryingplace was Samson buried?

answers: The number of years Samson judged Israel
The number of Philistines on the roof
The number of gates in Gaza
medium.explanation: The verse concludes by stating that Samson judged Israel twenty years.
medium.q: What does the verse mention besides the place of burial?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the members of his father’s household and family.
medium.q: What does “all the house of his father” mean here?

answers: His family buried him, and the verse summarizes his years of leadership
The Philistines buried him and ended their rule
His brothers appointed him judge after his death
challenge.explanation: The verse describes his burial and then summarizes his twenty years as judge.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the beginning and end of the verse?

answers: The burial place was between Zorah and Eshtaol
The tomb was in the valley of Sorek
challenge.explanation: The verse says he was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol.
challenge.q: What geographical detail appears in the burial account?

answers: The Philistines returned him to his family
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that his brethren and his father’s household took and buried him.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that his family carried him?
